post_title: What will the front-month Brent crude oil futures settlement price be on October 30, 2026?

question.title: What will the front-month Brent crude oil futures settlement price be on October 30, 2026?
question.description:
ICE Brent Crude is the leading global benchmark for crude oil pricing. Front-month (nearest-expiry) Brent futures settle each trading day on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), and the daily settlement is widely republished by financial data providers such as Barchart.

Brent has been exceptionally volatile in 2026, driven heavily by the Russia-Ukraine war and associated sanctions dynamics. Over the 52 weeks to mid-October 2026 the price ranged from roughly $59 to about $138 per barrel. The 2026 year-to-date average was about $93.81 (vs. $69.14 for 2025). As of October 16, 2026, front-month Brent settled around $109-110 per barrel, up sharply over the prior month.

Recent price drivers include: Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries (Kyiv claims more than half of Russia's refining capacity has been knocked out), a short-lived "energy ceasefire" announced by President Trump on October 11, 2026 and its breakdown, a US-Russia deal to allow Russian diesel back into the US ahead of midterm elections, and reports that Washington is weighing easing sanctions on the "shadow fleet" of vessels carrying Russian, Iranian, and Venezuelan oil. The IEA's October 2026 report noted sharp declines in Russian and Middle Eastern product exports. These overlapping geopolitical and supply factors make the near-term price path genuinely uncertain.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the settlement ("Last" / closing) price in US dollars per barrel of the front-month ICE Brent Crude Oil futures continuous contract on Friday, October 30, 2026, as reported on Barchart's historical price page for the continuous front-month Brent contract: https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CB*0/price-history/historical . For example, a settlement of $104.30 per barrel resolves as 104.3. The relevant value is the daily settlement for the trading date October 30, 2026.
question.fine_print: If October 30, 2026 is not a trading day for ICE Brent futures (e.g., an unexpected market closure), the question resolves to the settlement price on the most recent prior trading day. The front-month contract is the nearest-expiry ICE Brent futures contract trading on that date (expected to be the December 2026 contract). If Barchart is unavailable or does not display the value, the settlement price reported by other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) for the same front-month ICE Brent contract and date will be used. If ICE Brent futures are permanently discontinued and no settlement exists, the question is annulled.
